text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert - streaming-infer p99 latency breach detected. p99 has jumped to ~2300ms (goal 300ms). Start time ~10:12 UTC. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/streaming-infer/latency p95 also up, streaming stalls observed on several hosts. Auto-fallback didn’t trigger for some requests. Paging oncall now.

elaine (oncall): acked. I’m on it. grabbing traces + rollout status.

aj: logging into grafana, pulling live p50/p95/p99, can you drop the hot queries you ran?

elaine (oncall): quick checks:
```
# prometheus
rate(streaming_infer_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(streaming_infer_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```
results: p99 spike aligns with 10:12 window, hosts in us-west-2 most affected.

joel: seeing increased `request_wait_for_kv_cache` in logs, some hosts report large KV cache misses after a churn event ~10:10.

maya (cs): FYI AcmeCorp support ticket 3421 reported timeouts around 10:13 and one user reported partial streaming (data cut). They’re asking if this is degrading production.

elaine (oncall): customer impact: seems intermittent but real for streaming endpoints. Estimate ~2-3% of requests affected based on sampled traces. tagging SRE.

sre-bot: Created incident bridge https://bridge.redwood.internal/incident/INC-1712349991 and PagerDuty triggered to SRE primary.

aj: quick mitigations we can try now: 1) enable `fallback_to_sync` for streaming-infer for affected hosts 2) route new traffic away from nodes with high KV miss rate 3) temporarily enable heavier batching in dedicated pools to reduce stalls.

elaine (oncall): rolling a targeted traffic-shift to fallback variant for us-west-2 now (canary to 5% -> 25%).

joel: pushing config: `routing.policy=region_weight(us-west-2:0.75, fallback:0.25)` — applying to service.

elaine (oncall): applied. monitoring p99.

(30s later)

elaine (oncall): p99 dropped from 2300ms -> 420ms in the first minute after routing change. p95 down to 220ms.

aj: nice. still above SLO for p99 but much improved. continuing to re-route and investigate root cause.

joel: digging into KV cache churn: logs show a spike of `cache_evict` events coincident with a background re-partition job that ran at 10:09. That job touched model shards and caused temporary miss storms.

maya (cs): telling AcmeCorp we're mitigating and will follow up with RCA. they want ETA on full restoration.

elaine (oncall): ETA: hold on full fix until we complete safe rollback of re-partition job and cold-warm cache rebuild — might be ~30-45 mins. telling customers 1h window.

aj: next steps: 1) full rollback of the re-partition job (in progress) 2) increase KV cache prewarm on warmed hosts 3) post-incident: adjust job scheduling and add circuit-breaker to avoid mass evictions.

elaine (oncall): opening postmortem ticket INC-1712349991-PM and adding action items.

(12m later)

elaine (oncall): rollback complete, cache prewarm tasks started. p99 stabilized at ~310ms, p95 ~195ms. still watching for residual stalls.

joel: adding alert tweak: add a transient-suppression window for background jobs to avoid false positive routing flips; also add metric `kv_cache_miss_rate` to the alert rule to reduce noise.

maya (cs): AcmeCorp updated: they see recovery and will keep monitoring from their side. thanks for quick response.

elaine (oncall): closing immediate paging loop. leaving incident active for RCA and follow-ups. tagging owners: @joel (infra), @aj (runtime), @maya (cs) for communications. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident moved to status: mitigated. Bridge remains open for RCA. Remember to file postmortem within 72h.
